characters.name: Jake Malloy
characters.description: Dr. Robby's quasi-stepson. Running Gag: When Jake comes into the department to pick up his tickets to a music festival, he's given a condom by a member of the staff on two occasions. When Robby gives him the passes and then reaches into his pocket to give him something else, Jake states that he's already been given condoms. Robby is surprised and states that he was just going to give him some extra pocket money.Robby: Wait, are you having sex?Jake:(Grabbing the money and running)Thank you! Why Couldn't You Save Them?: Jake is quite upsetthat Robby couldn't save his girlfriend Leah and their relationship is badly fractured by the end of Season One as a result. You're Not My Father: AfterRobby fails to save LeahJake screams this at him as he tries to make up with him.

characters.name: Janey Malloy
characters.description: Amicable Exes: Robby and Janey have broken up, but Robby is still a quasi-paternal figure to Janey's son Jake. Janey also greets Robby affectionately when she comes to pick Jake up from the ER and even does her best to comfort him overLeah's death.

characters.name: Chad Ashcroft
characters.description: Dr.McKay's ex-husband, and father of their son Harrison. Age-Gap Romance: He's aboutMcKays's age (early-to-mid fourties), while his girlfriend is twenty-five. Driven by Envy: Whileunder the influence of heavy surgical anesthesia, it comes out that the reason Chad is so cold to Mateo is that he's envious of the man's youth, good looks, and easy relationship with his son. Jealousy is also a factor; he thinksMcKaymight be having sex with him (even thoughthe audience knows that Mateo doesn't date coworkers). Everyone Has Standards: After being a smugJerkassevery time he shows up,McKay's ex-husband Chad is horrified at the aftermath ofthe Pittfest shootingand seems to gain a new respect for her upon seeing her at work in the extremely stressful conditions. Jerkass: Smug and unpleasant towards his ex-wife and her co-workers the entire time he's in the ER, including Mateo who goes out of his way to try to be friendly to him. It is very little wonder that his son prefersMcKay.

characters.name: Harrison Ashcroft
characters.description: Dr.McKay's 11-year-old son, who ends up in the ER for the day when Chad has his skateboard accident. Momma's Boy: Due to Chad's irresponsible nature, Harrison clearly prefers being with his mother over being with his father. When Cassie mentions that Chad being laid up means that he could stay with her for a while, he gets so excited that he hugs her immediately. Sweet Tooth: Cassie mentions that Harrison loves smores and pizza, though she backtracks afterward to comment that she doesn't just feed him junk food. Wise Beyond Their Years: Harrison comes off as smarter than his father despite only being eleven.

characters.name: NeilMcKay
characters.description: Dr.McKay's dad, who appears briefly in Season 1. Doting Grandparent: What little we see of him indicates this - Harrison excitedly runs to him for a hug when he arrives, and we later find out that they end up watchingPlanet of the Apes (1968)together while waiting for Dr.McKayto finish her shift. Good Parents: Despite what she's been through, he still loves and supports his daughter.

characters.name: Becca King
characters.description: Dr. Mel King's autistic sister, who lives in an assisted living facility and who Mel has cared for and looked after for most of their lives. She ends up becoming a patient in Season 2 after contracting a UTI. Big Sister Worship: It's clear Becca admires Mel and her work a great deal, trusting Mel when she needs to go to the hospital and being impressed with the Pitt when she arrives. Brutal Honesty: Becca's autism leaves her a bit unfiltered and she expresses things more directly even when it's not polite, seen when she non-maliciously talks about the "smelly people" around her in the waiting room. She alsoexpectsdirect, specifically-worded honesty from others, shown in the way she asks Langdon not to tell her he'll "be back in a minute" unless he meansa minute. Hidden Depths: Mel is very shocked to find out Becca has a boyfriend whom she’s been sexually active with, leading to her UTI. Related to this, Becca also insists upon having her maturity and independence respected, politely but firmly correcting Mel when she identifies Becca not by her name but simply as "my sister" and later heading Mel off at the pass when she tries to over-explain the simple process of prepping for an examination at the hospital. Innocently Insensitive: Becca's autism means she's very blunt and direct. She also doesn't see that she's disregarding Mel's genuine concerns by not keeping her in the loop. Mel is genuinely heartbroken by Becca cutting off their usual plans of seeing the fireworks together, which Becca doesn't realize.
